title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: multicloud risk indicators
summary: Hold: the advice treats alert thresholds as a way to control processing charges, but the documentation checked does not establish that relationship. The licensing section also incorrectly says its cited section names no plan, although that section names Microsoft 365 Enterprise E5. The roadmap facts and the principal controls are supported; all cited Learn pages opened successfully.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans ready-to-use multicloud indicators for Azure, AWS, Box, Dropbox, Google Drive and GitHub.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management extends its detection into multicloud environments by offering ready-to-use risk indicators in Azure, AWS, and SaaS apps including Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, and GitHub.

claims.claim: The roadmap names data theft and data leaks policies as consumers of the indicators.
claims.quote: Organizations can use these new indicators in data theft and data leaks policies.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview billing models Insider Risk Management processing units'; opened purview-billing-models in full. Its Cost estimator tools section links to Microsoft pay-as-you-go pricing and the calculator; no numeric processing-unit price appears.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: Insider Risk Management processes activities for selected non-Microsoft 365 indicators in data theft and data leak policies to generate insights, alerts and cases.
claims.quote: Insider Risk Management processes user activities corresponding to the non-Microsoft 365 indicators selected in data theft and data leak policies to generate insights, alerts, and cases.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Cloud storage indicators can be turned off per app, for example enabling Box and Google Drive but not Dropbox.
claims.quote: After configuring the cloud storage indicators, you can turn off indicators for the apps you don't want to use in settings. For example, you can select a content download indicator for Box and Google Drive, but not Dropbox.

claims.claim: Policy indicators determine risk scores for in-scope users and produce alerts for review.
claims.quote: Indicators included in Insider Risk Management policies determine a risk score for an in-scope user. You enable policy indicators from indicators defined in global settings. The policy indicators activate only after a triggering event occurs for a user.

claims.claim: The cloud storage indicators detect discovery, collection, exfiltration and deletion activity.
claims.quote:
Use cloud storage indicators to detect the following activities in Google Drive, Box, and Dropbox:

- Discovery: Techniques used to figure out the environment
- Collection: Techniques used to gather data of interest
- Exfiltration: Techniques used to steal data, such as sensitive documents

claims.claim: Amazon S3 and Azure cloud service indicators detect defence evasion, exfiltration, deletion and privilege escalation.
claims.quote: Defense evasion: Techniques used to avoid detection of risky activities by disabling trace logs or by updating or deleting SQL Server firewall rules

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Adjusting indicator thresholds affects alert volume.
claims.quote: The guided experience helps you efficiently adjust the selection of indicators and thresholds for activity occurrences so you don't have too few or too many policy alerts.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A low alert threshold can raise the Azure bill, and setting thresholds deliberately limits processing-unit use.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Insider Risk Management cloud indicators thresholds reduce processing units billing'; read purview-billing-models, settings-policy-indicators and reports. They document activity-based processing charges and alert thresholds, but not this asserted cost relationship.
claims.fix: Replace 'Billing follows usage, so a low threshold on a busy app can raise both alert volume and the Azure bill.' with 'Billing follows processed user activities; indicator thresholds affect alert volume.' In the At rollout bullet, replace 'set thresholds deliberately rather than leaving defaults, to limit processing-unit use' with 'set thresholds deliberately to tune alert volume'.

claims.where: Scope: Who and what; Why it matters
claims.claim: The data theft by departing users template can include Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, Amazon S3 and Azure indicators.
claims.quote: This can include cloud indicators for services such as Box, Dropbox, Google Drive, Amazon S3, and Azure.

claims.where: Scope: Clouds and platform; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The cloud-indicator Learn pages read do not specify which government clouds support these indicators.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Insider Risk Management GCC High DoD cloud indicators pay-as-you-go availability'; read configure and settings-policy-indicators cloud sections and GCC High deployment table. No feature-specific government-cloud coverage statement found.

claims.claim: The GCC High deployment page's Insider Risk Management rows name no cloud storage or cloud service indicators.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Insider Risk Management GitHub cloud indicators GCC GCC High DoD availability'; opened plan-for-microsoft-purview-gcc-high-deployments and read all Insider Risk Management rows. They name Office and other indicators, not cloud storage or cloud service indicators.

claims.claim: An Insider Risk Management pay-as-you-go usage report is available under Reports.
claims.quote:
The following reports are available by navigating to Insider Risk Management > Reports in the Microsoft Purview portal:

- Pay-as-you-go: Review pay-as-you-go usage reports to identify cost-saving opportunities and fine-tune your policy configurations.

claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go report identifies usage across data source categories and activity indicators.
claims.quote: The reports let you explore granular breakdowns of billed processing usage across different data source categories and activity indicators over time.

claims.claim: No single documented switch turns the multicloud capability on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Insider Risk Management multicloud indicators enable disable single switch settings'; read configure, settings-policy-indicators and billing-usage. Found app connections, individual/global indicator selection and billing prerequisites, not a dedicated multicloud switch.

claims.claim: The Policy indicators page says globally selected indicators cannot be individually configured while creating or editing a policy.
claims.quote: The indicators you select on the Policy indicators settings page can't be individually configured when creating or editing an insider risk policy in the policy workflow.
claims.fix: Remove this sentence to avoid presenting one side of conflicting documentation. The already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-configure#step-6-required-create-an-insider-risk-management-policy also says 'Select the indicators you want to apply to the policy' and describes custom policy indicator thresholds.

claims.claim: Disabling policy indicators in global settings stops their use across insider risk policies.
claims.quote: You can turn off the policy indicators for specific areas by disabling them from all insider risk policies in global settings.

claims.claim: Disabling an app connector stops its ingestion and is a route to reduce incoming activity.
claims.quote: Once disabled, the connector instance stops consuming data from the connector.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects usage-based processing-unit charges rather than a fixed included cost.
claims.quote: For Insider Risk Management, a processing unit represents the compute required to process 10,000 such user activities. Billing is based on the number of processing units utilized.

claims.claim: Every control that the governance checklist asks the reader to configure or check appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: The checklist says 'confirm the tenant is associated with it', 'Add the indicators to a data theft or data leaks policy' and 'Review the pay-as-you-go usage report'; the table covers indicator settings, app connections, Usage center and role membership.
claims.fix: The Before rollout Azure-subscription association check, At rollout policy configuration and threshold step, and After rollout Insider Risk Management Reports check have no corresponding control rows. The claim that no single multicloud switch exists is likewise not represented by a both-null row.

claims.claim: The roadmap record states no rollout default for the multicloud indicators.
claims.quote: Searched: the supplied roadmap record's description and fields for a multicloud rollout default. The only 'by default' passage concerns user pseudonymization, not indicator activation; no rollout-default field or statement is present.
